chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa and Ibn Abi Umeyr, all together from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The blood of istihada (inter-period bleeding) and haydh (menstruation) do not come out from one place. The blood of istihada is cold, and the blood of haydh is hot.'

key_terms.الاسْتِحَاضَةِ: Istihada: inter-period bleeding or non-menstrual uterine bleeding
key_terms.بَارِدٌ: Cold (referring to the nature of istihada blood)
key_terms.حَارٌّ: Hot (referring to the nature of menstrual blood)

ai.seo_question: How to distinguish between menstrual blood and inter-period bleeding based on temperature and origin?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between menstrual blood (haydh) and inter-period bleeding (istihada) by their origin and temperature. He states that they do not exit from the same place, noting that istihada blood is cold while menstrual blood is hot.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Hammad Bin Isa and Ibn Abu Umeyr, altogether from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The blood of the inter-period bleeding (Istihaaza) and the menstruation (Haydh) do not come out from one place. The blood of the inter-period bleeding (Istihaaza) is cold, and the blood of the menstruation (Haydh) is hot’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa and ibn abu ‘Umayr all from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Blood discharge because of Istihadah (irregular menses) and Hayd (menses) does not come from the same place. Blood discharge because of Istihadah (irregular menses) is cold, and because of Hayd (menses) it is hot.’”
